result.title: Regularization Amplifies Subliminal Learning
result.summary: Recent work has shown that hidden biases can be transferred through data with no apparent semantic relationship to those biases. Can regularization limit this covert influence? By constraining adaptation, regularization might be expected to suppress behavioral changes on seemingly unrelated inputs. We systematically study this hypothesis in subliminal learning, as well as in related settings of covert influence, including phantom transfer and logit-linear selection. We find the opposite: regularization amplifies the transfer of hidden biases. In particular, subliminal learning is typically absent under full fine-tuning, but low-rank adaptation or explicit penalties can induce strong transfer. Phantom transfer and logit-linear selection show similar trends. Adding more data, an implicit form of regularization, also strengthens covert influence. Together, these findings suggest that the simplicity biases induced by regularization may facilitate covert influence. We further hypothesize that the level of regularization that maximizes covert transfer depends on task complexity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文系统检验正则化能否抑制 subliminal learning 等隐蔽影响，结果发现相反：全参数微调下几乎不出现隐藏偏置迁移，而 LoRA 或显式惩罚等限制适应的手段反而放大迁移，增加数据量也有类似效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于低秩约束、简单性偏置如何让与任务语义无关的信息沿训练信号传播的观察，可能为核查 LVR 训练中的监督归因与信息坍缩提供线索，但该工作属纯行为与训练层面研究，未涉及视觉推理。
